title: Start journeys from the reference strategy; justify alternatives

facts.note: Discovery signal: task text mentions journey execution, a strategy name, or a requirement axis that motivates strategy choice. Not a standalone firing condition.
Needs an observer that knows the agent is authoring a plan/wagon/WMBT/acceptance rather than implementing.

values: journey execution strategy selected, changed or combined (any strategy to any other)
facts.note: Diff-level observer over journey plan artifacts is required to detect any strategy selection or revision.

values: non-reference strategy considered or chosen without requirement or measured-workload justification
facts.note: Diagnostic only, used to report non-compliance after the rule has fired; NOT an activation prerequisite. The rule fires on every journey strategy selection or revision.

fires: Planner authors a new journey and selects how its steps execute (reference or any alternative/combination).
Planner revises an existing journey's strategy in any direction: reference to alternative, alternative to another alternative, alternative back to reference, or adding a combined strategy.
Strategy change is motivated by latency, throughput, cost, reliability, determinism or complexity concerns.
Plan proposes fork/join, streaming or speculation that the runtime may not yet support.
doesNotFire: A wagon optimizes its own internals without changing journey control flow.
Edits to a journey that do not touch its execution strategy (e.g. renaming, doc wording).
Coder implementing an already-accepted plan with no strategy decision to make.

given: A plan defines or revises a journey's execution strategy; strategies are candidate ways to meet declared behavioral obligations.
when: The planner selects, changes or combines strategies.
then: Begin with the reference strategy, then consider alternatives or combinations only when latency, throughput, cost, reliability, determinism or complexity requirements, or measured workloads, justify their complexity.
prefer: Treat strategies as orthogonal, combinable candidates; none is universally best. The baseline is the reference strategy convention (planner.journey.strategy.reference).
Keep ownership: interlockings select guarded alternatives, journeys compose control flow, trains stay linear, wagons optimize internals.
Plan only behavior the plan and runtime actually support; preserve contracts, artifacts, prerequisites, side effects, error paths and terminal outcomes.
Prove equivalence with behavioral tests; back performance claims with reproducible benchmarks.
avoid: Exploring alternatives without a requirement or measured workload that justifies the complexity.
Using a strategy choice to bypass interlockings, trains, continuations or acceptances.
Assuming fork/join, stream or speculation exists; missing capability needs separate implementation and accepted proof.
Slipping observable behavior changes in via a strategy; they need their own accepted route.
why: Alternatives add complexity and risk to behavior that must stay equivalent. This is Bun-owned advisory planner guidance, not a new runtime mode or independently enforced rule; existing journey, interlocking and acceptance validators stay authoritative.
evidence: Reviewer can establish that the journey began from the reference strategy and that any alternative or combination considered is justified by a latency, throughput, cost, reliability, determinism or complexity requirement or by a measured workload.
Behavioral tests show the alternative preserves contracts, artifacts, prerequisites, side effects, error paths and terminal outcomes.
Performance claims are backed by reproducible benchmarks.
Every used capability (fork/join, stream, speculation) is supported by the plan and runtime or has a separate implementation with accepted proof.
Existing journey, interlocking and acceptance validators still pass; they remain authoritative.
verifier_detail: Advisory, severity 3: not independently enforced and not a new runtime mode; report as guidance, defer to existing journey, interlocking and acceptance validators.
Requirement axes to check a justification against: latency, throughput, cost, reliability, determinism, complexity; measured workloads are also an accepted justification.
